title: Radical Acceptance
subtitle: Featuring our friend Vint Blackburn, M.D.
body_html:
The Frontier Psychiatrists— it's a newsletter, and more. Today, I'm sharing a meditation on radical acceptance, and featuring a video from my friend Dr. Vint Blackburn.

Vint goes a little dark on this one, and offers an example of how hard radical acceptance can be, while still functioning as a core coping skill in a difficult world.

He explains, better than I will—so please like and subscribe to his videos!—that radical acceptance isn't about liking what's happening. It isn't about getting over something awful. He describes the radicalness as related to accepting what is. What is now…is. It's not about making it less painful. It's not about coping in some magical way with things that painful and no one could ever get over. It's about acknowledging the moment, and moving forward.

He provides examples, and I'm gonna riff off one of his so that you still want to watch his video.

Imagine you are on your way to pick up a lottery ticket. Somebody, in advance, called you and told you that lottery ticket was the winner. All you have to do is walk in, put down a dollar, pick up the ticket, and the next day every financial war you've ever had would be over. It’s in another city. You buy a plane ticket.

On the way there, you get to the airport, only to find out that there's been a tornado that's ripped the entire thing apart. There's no way you can drive. There is no way you can fly. The opportunity to change your life has been a completely and utterly taken away from you.

You could sit down, give up, throw your hands in the air, scream, and all of that might be comforting in the moment. None of it would be useful in moving forward from that loss. You were about to have no worry about money again, and thanks to a freak tornado, your “good luck” has turned to ashes. There is no option that involves picking up the ticket. There is no way to win in the way you thought you were going to. The only thing you get to do is decide what else you're going to do, and what your relationship will be to this loss going forward.

It's not about changing what happened. That's never gonna change. It's about deciding on your relationship with the future, no matter what happened in the past, or what happened in this moment. No one's ever going force you to be OK with it, but you do get to decide but the next moment attitude is, and the next, and the next.

He highlights at the end that even those who are about to have the guillotine come down? They decide they react to that very last moment.

A lot of the forces in our life are beyond our control. The most important things that will ever happen to us, almost uniformly, or not because of our volition, choices, or strength, or wisdom, or great judgment.

You don't get to choose who you love, what unimaginable tragedies befall you, remarkable wins come your way. The only real decision we have to make is how we orient ourselves to the next moment.

I'm grateful to Vint for sharing this video with me, And I hope you can share this article with people who need it, because that's everybody at some point.

Thanks for reading.
